scenes.text: Meet Cues. Context you declare. Behaviour that ends.
Your day is full of small moments. Earbuds go in, and you want focus. Starting a routine is easy. Trusting it, and knowing when it stops, is the hard part.
With Cues, you just say it. When my earbuds connect after six P M on weekdays, start a forty-five minute focus timer, and quiet notifications. End it if I disconnect.
Before anything is armed, Cues shows the whole story. When. If. Do. Until. And restore. You see how it starts, how it ends, and what it releases. Then you approve that exact version.
A small local model drafts the cue, but it never runs anything. Its output is validated, and you approve it. Below that line, only ordinary Android code runs, with no model in the loop.

Then comes the part most tools skip: the ending. Disconnect your earbuds, and the session ends. Cues releases only what it owns. If another mode still needs quiet, it stays quiet. A receipt explains why.
You can rehearse a cue first, on clearly labelled sample events, and see which would start, which would be skipped, and why.

Phones are getting deeply contextual. Siri A I in iOS twenty-seven infers context from your messages and screen. That is powerful, and we do not claim to beat it. Cues takes the other road. Context is declared, not inferred. You choose the signals, and everything else stays unknown.
This is a proposal for a focused prototype: Bluetooth and charging first, with a real start, and a real ending. Cues. Context you declare. Behaviour that ends.
